summary: Empty optional notes survive saved-file reload; malformed, invalid-precision and duplicate records reject the whole load without an exit-time overwrite.
Saving validates and serializes before writing a temporary sibling and atomically replacing the destination, with failed-move cleanup.
Complete CRUD adds immutable replacement updates and confirmed CLI deletion; failed commands preserve existing state and totals.
Shared domain precision/category validation, guarded ID allocation, snapshot loading and graceful EOF strengthen the foundational service boundaries.
A portable Java 17 runner and nine detailed learning documents cover actual source, failure traces, worked changes, regression reasoning and progressive CRUD web API exercises.

checks.environment: Microsoft OpenJDK 17.0.10; --release 17 -Xlint:all; real temporary files; isolated project copy

limits: CLI only; HTTP, browser UI, database and authenticated owner scoping are proposed exercises.
Save-on-exit can lose unsaved edits after forced termination; no cross-process coordination or power-loss durability guarantee.
IDs can be reused after deleting the highest record and restarting; exhaustion does not wrap.
Atomic replacement is required; unsupported filesystems fail visibly. Strict loading requires manual repair of corrupt copies.
CLI diagnostics are printed; structured failure exit codes are not yet implemented.
